title: FRESHO: a same-Wi-Fi paint war built with Claude Code (trailer, web build, and what I learned)
author: Beautiful-Today-2166
selftext:
\*\*Trailer:\*\* [https://youtu.be/InjNqggXobc](https://youtu.be/InjNqggXobc)

\*\*Play it (browser, Windows, VR):\*\* [https://isthisrequired.itch.io/fresho](https://isthisrequired.itch.io/fresho)



\*\*FRESHO\*\* is a top-down paint war. Every step you take paints the map in your team's colour. Your own paint speeds you up and heals you, enemy paint slows you down, and the whole war is a fight over the ground itself.



\### What's in it

\- \*\*13 animal heroes\*\* in a rubber-hose cartoon style, each with a gun, an ability and a super. Among them: a raccoon with a drum-fed ray SMG, a crow sniper, a bear boxer, and a penguin butler who belly-slides through crowds.

\- \*\*2 to 60 fighters on up to 7 teams\*\*, with bots filling every empty slot.

\- \*\*9 modes.\*\* My favourites are \*Lasso\* (close a loop of paint and everything inside flips to your colour), \*Last Colour\* (a rising cutoff knocks teams out) and \*Paint Tide\* (the paint grows like Game of Life cells).

\- \*\*6 worlds\*\*, plus fortress breaches, orbital strikes, destructible cover, springboards and vending machines.

\- \*\*Same-Wi-Fi multiplayer\*\* on PC, Android and browser. No accounts and no servers: one device hosts, and everyone in the room joins.



\### How it was built

I directed the design and Claude Code wrote the code:

\- \*\*Engine:\*\* Three.js, with a toon shader and an ink-outline post pass.

\- \*\*Art:\*\* every 3D model comes from a Python script run headless in Blender. There's no asset store and no AI image generation; it's all procedural modelling.

\- \*\*Audio:\*\* fully synthesized in WebAudio, music included. There isn't a single audio file in the game.

\- \*\*Networking:\*\* UDP discovery on the LAN, a WebSocket relay in the native apps, and WebRTC when a browser hosts. The native .exe and .apk are thin shells around the web build.

\- \*\*Trailer:\*\* cut from the real game. It runs headless on the GPU in slow motion and frames are grabbed at exact game times. Each clip's sound is the game's own audio replayed from that clip's event log.



\### What I learned working with AI on a game this size

\- \*\*Tests are the AI's eyes.\*\* The project has an automated suite of about 50 steps: bot matches, headless-browser screenshots, LAN tests with real server processes, and audio checks. Without it, every change was a guess.

\- \*\*Be specific about feel.\*\* "Make it better" got me nowhere. "The territory edges must be fluid and the inside coloured everywhere, no gaps" worked.



Happy to answer anything about the workflow. Feedback on the trailer and the game is very welcome 🙏
